answer: Persistent puzzle escrow. Each identity must solve a fresh computational puzzle whose solution seeds a slow memory-hard chain; the resulting ridge of verified work history is registered to that identity alone. To forge a second identity, an attacker must rerun the full chain from scratch at real hardware cost, since solutions cannot be copied or merged across identities. Every new account therefore pays the entire accumulated proof cost again, and any attempt to reuse an anchor from a prior identity is rejected.
